title: Zariski square-zero ring-sheaf extensions with marked kernel and base
statement: Let $f:X\to B$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $G$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [pqf-def-coherent]. A Zariski square-zero extension of $\mathcal O_X$ by $G$ over $B$ consists of a sheaf $\mathcal E$ of commutative unital rings on $|X|$, a ring-sheaf map $p:\mathcal E\to\mathcal O_X$, and an additive sheaf map $i:G\to\mathcal E$ such that $i$ is injective, its image is the kernel of $p$, and $p$ is locally surjective. For every open $U$, $i(m)i(n)=0$ and $i(p(a)m)=a i(m)$ for sections $a,m,n$. The base algebra structure is a ring-sheaf map $\mathcal O_B\to f_*\mathcal E$ whose composite with $f_*p$ is $f^\sharp$; by adjunction this is the $f^{-1}\mathcal O_B$-algebra structure. Its ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] is $(|X|,\mathcal E)$, its reduction is $(\mathrm{id},p)$, and its base map has point map $|f|$ and sheaf map the specified base action. A marked realization is a scheme $Y$, an isomorphism of ringed spaces $e:Y\cong(|X|,\mathcal E)$, and arrows $j:X\to Y$, $q:Y\to B$ with $j$ a first order thickening [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], $j q=f$, $e j=(\mathrm{id},p)$ and the induced base arrow equal to $q$. An extension map is a ringed-space arrow with identity point map, commuting with these quotient and base maps; its sheaf map runs contravariantly.
